title: Independence of the normalized rational point tensor map
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l distinct from its characteristic, a finite coefficient field E/Q_l, and point tensor systems S1 and S2 over possibly different algebraic closures of Q_l [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-system]. Suppose each system admits the specified canonical finite, full Roos-coordinate integral, scalar-localization and carrier normalizations [def-pod-point-fibre-tensor-canonical]. For any bounded constructible rational point complexes M,N, the rational tensor-comparison morphisms of S1 and S2 at E are heterogeneously equal. This asserts equality of normalized comparison maps, not existence of a tensor system.

proof.text: On finite K-flat models the normalized tensor comparisons send every pure tensor of sections to the same pure tensor. Sheaf tensor generators span the maps, so the induced chain maps agree.

source.place: Final smooth-pairing clause; retained rational point-pairing argument, Steps 1--7.

proof.text: Use the integral normalization before localization: the two comparisons are inverses of the same completed augmentation, whose first Roos coordinate is the quotient tensor and whose second coordinate is zero. Hence the product/cone maps agree, including their cone coordinate. No faithfulness of individual quotient reductions is required.

proof.text: The rational normalization is the image of this map under balanced scalar tensor and its specified counit. The carrier lift uses the prescribed pure-tensor tensorator, so the lifted maps agree on complexes and roofs; faithfulness of the carrier lift reflects the equality. This calculation depends only on E, and therefore gives the same morphism for the two closure presentations.
